A thoughtfully delivered zinger is a potent tool. It can swiftly de-escalate a cumbersome, overly signaling situation. Is there anyone who doesn't feel relaxed when an office jester makes light of their mistake? In a meeting with a group that’s approaching my territory, I once used humor to let the group know that I intended to be “administering policy” rather than in a “selling” role. When I first learned of a key hire who was not gender diverse, I inquired of the person who was my supervisor about it. He said, “You’ll like him.” Without even a moment to breathe I had responded: “You know me too well,” an awkward moment avoided.
Working on Wall Street, I learned about humor from the very top. I had the privilege to sit across from the legendary leader
